not_a_topline: This adds and replaces no topline row. It records what the keep-mask costs at 262,144 positions, what a mask-free derived-causal path costs, and why the derived path was reverted rather than landed. benchmarks/README.md is unchanged.
recorded: 2026-10-02, gfx1151 Strix Halo (zbook, AMD Radeon 8060S, 124 GB unified), Gemma 4 26B-A4B UD-Q4_K_XL
why: The previous unit made 262,144 positions runnable at 998.1 s for a 262,140-token prefill. The follow-up premise was that the runtime's dense (rows, keys) uint8 keep-mask was a large part of that: 512 x 260,608 = 133 MB per full-layer block, ~342 GB across a prefill. The arithmetic was right and the conclusion was wrong, and the cost of acting on it was measured before and after the change.

mask_cost_measured.method: _keep_mask(geometry, start, rows) called directly on the real geometries, host wall clock, no GPU. Summed over every 512-row block of a 262,144-token prefill for both layer geometries, as the runner does it (once per distinct sliding_window).
mask_cost_measured.note: The sliding layer's mask is 0.8 MB rather than 134 MB because _sliding_read_range trims the band to window + rows - 1 columns, so only the 5 full layers pay.

kernel_ab.method: same device buffers, same arguments, both arms alternated within one process so thermal drift shows in both; 2 warmup launches per arm; median of N
kernel_ab.arms: explicit (the caller's mask is passed and read) against derived (null pointer, kernel computes key_position <= row_position and the window term)

rows.after: the derived comparison narrowed from int64_t to int

kernel_ab.finding: Deriving is slower than reading, and most of the gap was the implementation: a 64-bit compare is three scalar instructions on this ISA where a 32-bit compare is one, which this codebase already documents for first_kept and walk_end. Narrowing to int halved the regression from 4.5 percent to 2.0 percent. The remaining 2 percent is the branch between the two paths inside the unrolled key loop.

end_to_end.protocol: hipengine.LLM(model=artifact, max_sequence_length=262144), a 262,140-token prompt from scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py's corpus, SamplingParams(max_tokens=4, temperature=0.0, ignore_eos=True)
end_to_end.reading: Same ids, so the derived path is correct end to end. The 18.5 percent wall gap is larger than the micro-benchmark predicts and is not explained; one sample per arm, with construction times of 20.6 s and 16.9 s showing an 18 percent spread between them. The decision rests on the micro-benchmark, not on this pair.

decision.reason: The walk is about 75 percent of a 256K prefill and the mask is 0.6 percent, so +2 percent on the walk costs about 15 s against the 6.4 s saved. Net negative. Closing the remaining 2 percent would need the key loop specialized on whether the mask is derived, which is real kernel complexity and a second parity surface, and its ceiling is the 6.4 s it saves.
decision.tree_state: at the base commit; the change was reverted from a saved patch after the measurement

correctness_of_the_reverted_path.why_recorded: It bounds what a future attempt would have to re-establish, and it separates 'this was wrong' from 'this was not worth it'.
correctness_of_the_reverted_path.method: each kernel run twice on identical buffers, once with the caller's mask and once with null, asserting explicit.view(uint32) == derived.view(uint32) -- bit-identical, not within tolerance
correctness_of_the_reverted_path.shapes_covered: tokens 512/512/512/512/1/16 against keys 512/4096/2048/2048/4096/40, with row_offset 0/3584/1024/1536/4095/24 and window 512/4096/1024/512/4096/40, including a window narrower than the block, a one-token decode, and keys < K_BATCH
correctness_of_the_reverted_path.result: all pass, alongside all 44 pre-existing parity tests in those two files
correctness_of_the_reverted_path.end_to_end: identical generated ids to the baseline

prefill_decomposition_at_256k.basis: non-attention from the 8,188-token prefill measured at 1,092 tok/s in the same session; attention FLOP from sum over blocks of 512 rows x 512(b+1) keys x 5 full layers x 16 heads x 2 x 512 dims
prefill_decomposition_at_256k.reading: The long-context cost is the 5 full layers' key walk, which grows with each block's own position, and it runs at about 7.5 TFLOP/s. That is what a long-context unit should be aimed at, not the mask.

limits: Device validation is gfx1151 only; no gfx1100 claim. The 6.4 s mask figure is for this geometry, this block size and this host, and it is quadratic in context, so re-measure before assuming it. The end-to-end pair is one sample per arm and is reported as measured rather than as the basis for the decision. The 7.5 TFLOP/s attention figure is derived from an estimated non-attention split, not from a profiler trace.
